nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node is over-crediting the edit: the edited image shows two white disc-like objects, while the source has one small rectangular DVD case/card near the center and a separate black object at right. The traces repeatedly assert that the DVD is white and preserved, but do not establish which edited object corresponds to the source DVD; the apparent white disc at center-left may be a newly introduced object, and the right-hand white disc appears on the dark object. Tighten the binding to track the specific source DVD across images and require direct evidence of its color change and retained DVD identity, rather than treating any white disc plus disc-like shape as fulfillment. Preserve the rubric’s partial/unresolved distinctions when correspondence or identity is uncertain; do not infer “no” solely from the reference label. The repeated high-confidence identical passes indicate a systematic grounding/binding or criterion-application problem, not a transport or schema failure.
s2: Repair the binding so it follows the specific source DVD across the before/after images, using its location and surrounding scene context—not merely any disc-like object in the edited image. The source shows a small rectangular item near the center and a separate dark object at right; the edit shows two white disc-like objects, so correspondence is ambiguous. Keep this identity check distinct from the requested black-to-white change: assess whether the matched source object remains recognizably a DVD, and do not treat whiteness or a central hole alone as proof of either correspondence or completion. Require evidence tied to the matched object; if correspondence or identity is indeterminate, preserve the rubric’s unresolved/partial distinctions rather than confidently passing. The repeated high-confidence passes point to a systematic grounding or criterion-application issue, not a transport/schema failure. Do not force the reference label to determine the node’s result.
s1: Repair the binding to track the specific source DVD across the before/after images using its position and scene context, rather than accepting any white disc-like object. In the source, the small rectangular item near the center is distinct from the dark object at right; the edit shows a white disc near center-left and another over the right-side object. The traces do not establish which, if either, corresponds to the source DVD. Require evidence that identifies the matched object as the original DVD and separately assesses its color; whiteness or a central hole alone proves neither correspondence nor retained identity. Preserve the rubric’s partial or unresolved outcomes when identity or progress is indeterminate, and do not force a result from the reference label. Repeated high-confidence passes indicate a systematic grounding/binding or criterion-application issue, not a transport or schema failure.
